newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy promises full probe into Albanian shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: Italy promises full probe into Albanian shipwreck.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday that Italy wanted a full investigation into the fatal sinking of an Albanian ship in the Adriatic and suggested both countries join forces in it.

"The government wants to clear this up completely, absolutely, so that no shadow of a doubt remains," he told reporters. "I am in favour of a bilateral Italo-Albanian effort to clarify thoroughly the facts."

Prodi said he would answer questions in the lower house of Parliament on Wednesday after Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta appeared in the Senate (upper house) on Tuesday to report on the tragedy.
He said he had asked Andreatta to inform his Albanian counterpart that "we are ready to work together. There must not be any problems or dramas between our two countries."

Tirana says 83 people are feared dead after an Albanian harbour patrol vessel crowded with refugees from the southern Albanian port of Vlore capsized and sank after colliding with an Italian navy ship trying to turn it away on Friday.

The shipwreck came as Rome was preparing to lead a multinational force of troops and police to secure key ports and protect aid deliveries in the lawless Balkan country torn by violence after the failure of risky savings schemes.
